message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc serves technology innovators as a design enablement partner, connecting design, emulation and test solutions across the full product lifecycle for customers in AI infrastructure, communications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductor and general electronics [D1]. In the quarter ended 2026-07-31 the company reported revenue of 1.85 billion dollars, net income of 397 million dollars and earnings per share of 2.82 against an estimate of 2.16, a surprise of 30.56 per cent [D1]. Revenue rose 36.54 per cent from a year earlier and 7.51 per cent from the quarter before, while net income rose 107.85 per cent from a year earlier [D1]. Gross margin was 65.87 per cent and net margin was 21.51 per cent [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of 1.35 billion dollars and operating income of 458 million dollars, and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of 501 million dollars and operating income of 155 million dollars [D1]. Total assets were 11.92 billion dollars, shareholders equity was 6.57 billion dollars and net debt was 141 million dollars [D1].

Management guided the fourth quarter of 2026 to revenue of 1.93 billion dollars to 1.95 billion dollars, earnings per share of 3.34 to 3.40 and a weighted diluted share count of 172 million shares, with the revenue mid-point representing growth of about 37 per cent [D1]. The report described the quarter as the second consecutive record quarter and tied the demand to the scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem [D1]. Management said wireline orders more than doubled from a year earlier, that wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time and that it expects orders slightly up from the prior quarter [D3]. Management described the funnel as an all-time high and said integration work on the recent acquisitions is largely complete [D3]. The company is positioning with hyperscalers beyond traditional capital expenditure into pre-silicon emulation and workload solutions [D4]. Keysight announced a research collaboration with the Centre for Assuring Autonomy at the University of York to advance practical methods for validating AI systems in software-defined vehicles [D7].

The argument in the market turns on how much of that demand converts into revenue, because management called the supply chain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters and said the supply environment is less flexible than a year earlier [D3]. Management said demand is not the limiter, that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear and that it is working with suppliers to deconstrain the supply chain [D3]. Management cautioned that the tariff impacts this year will not repeat and leave a high comparison bar for profitability [D3]. Analysts pressed on the sustainability of order levels and on whether guidance is capped by supply, a tone the summary described as pressing [D3]. The mix of the wireline business has shifted toward manufacturing as AI data centre build-outs scale, and internal capacity constraints for new product ramps have largely been resolved while external component supply remains the constraint [D4].

The latest report was published after the close on 2026-08-18 and the shares moved -6.32 per cent in the session of 2026-08-19 [D2]. The largest five-session move measured 28.62 per cent into the session of 2026-02-24, and a five-session decline of 13.98 per cent ran into 2026-08-24 [D2]. The write-up on analyst price targets argues that a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides, and that analysts often set overly optimistic targets to drum up interest in shares their firms have existing relationships with or seek to be associated with [D5]. The same write-up says the consensus estimate for the current year moved higher with no negative revision and that the shares carry a strong buy ranking on that basis [D5].
